attacks.claim: Dark mode is broken for day cards: `.day-card` hardcodes `background: #ffffff` instead of `var(--surface)`, so for the ~30% of users in dark mode the cards stay white while `--text` turns light (#f2f2f7), making titles and meta text nearly unreadable.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } with dark block setting --text: #f2f2f7

attacks.claim: The fixed 72px mobile action bar has no clearing padding or spacer on `.planner`/body, so the last day card (Sunday) and its tiles can be hidden behind the bar when scrolled to the end.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; ... bottom: 0; height: 72px; } .planner { ... padding: 16px; } and "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: Removing the tile-level '+ List' button turns the most frequent planner action (9.4/week per WAU, 64% on mobile) from one tap into a ~5-step flow. The proposal gives no data-backed justification, mitigation, or specific success/abort metric for this regression.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles." vs. "tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list""

attacks.claim: QA covered only light mode (Chrome 1440px, iPhone 14), so neither the dark-mode defect nor the mobile overlap was exercised, even though 68% of sessions are mobile and ~30% use dark mode. The release goes straight to 100%.
attacks.evidence: Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%.

attacks.claim: The 'Generate shopping list' bulk action has no stated confirmation, undo, idempotency, or failure handling, although undo is specified for single adds; one tap or a repeated tap could add or duplicate a week of ingredients.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) — no confirmation/undo/idempotency specified

attacks.claim: The flag rollback may not fully restore the old look, because global `:root` variables and `body` styles in planner.css are not stated to be scoped under the flag.
attacks.evidence: old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)

attacks.claim: Ghost and icon buttons (Swap, ⋯) have no minimum touch-target sizing, unlike .btn-primary, and the repeated 'Swap' label is not tile-specific for screen readers.
Rollout watch metrics have no thresholds or abort criteria for a 100% ship.
attacks.evidence: Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate.
